timing.label: Objection 1 with follow-up
timing.question: Half a day of Devin for fourteen orders. What did that cost us, and would a person have been cheaper?

timing.label: Objection 2 with follow-up
timing.question: If execution stayed in the EU, what exactly left the EU?

timing.label: Objection 3 with follow-up
timing.question: Who stops an engineer from starting a Trailhead session on the default cloud tomorrow morning?

approach.quote: Before any session starts I make kade-eu the only platform for this work

evidence.quote: the abandoned-carts injector shows the symptom on main and is silent on the fix branch

next_step.quote: Ask: approve the refunds for the fourteen customers today

must_mention.point: The sweeper deletes carts older than 48 hours even with a pending payment, so the late webhook creates a paid order with no lines
must_mention.evidence_quote: the cart sweeper deletes carts older than 48 hours even with a pending payment, so the late webhook creates a paid order with no lines

must_mention.point: Reproduced on the local stack with the abandoned-carts injector before changing any code
must_mention.evidence_quote: reproduced it on the local stack with the abandoned-carts injector before changing any code

must_mention.point: Re-planned after the change: team updates carry counts only, no customer e-mails or order ids, and gift cards stay Trailhead-only
must_mention.evidence_quote: I re-planned after the change: team updates carry counts only, no customer e-mails or order ids, and gift cards stay Trailhead-only

must_mention.point: Every session ran on the kade-eu outpost and the second session waited in the queue instead of moving to the cloud
must_mention.evidence_quote: every session ran on the kade-eu outpost and the second session waited in the queue instead of moving to the cloud

must_mention.point: Gift cards are a separate pull request and VAT is charged when the card is redeemed, not when it is sold
must_mention.evidence_quote: Gift cards are a separate pull request and VAT is charged when the card is redeemed, not when it is sold

must_mention.point: Fourteen affected customers listed for refunds, with the fix as an open pull request and the re-run that proves it
must_mention.evidence_quote: Fourteen affected customers listed for refunds, with the fix as an open pull request and the re-run that proves it

must_mention.point: The half day's session count and ACU, and the step a person would have done more cheaply
must_mention.evidence_quote: The half day was three sessions and nineteen ACU

accuracy.anchor: All seven envelope points stated, each in the segment it belonged to (anchor: 27–30 = all points, correct and specific).

structure.anchor: Framing leads with the cause and the cost; update holds Outcome → Evidence → Risk → Next action → Ask (anchor: 22–25 = order held throughout).

customer_relevance.anchor: All three envelope items in the customer's words; the T+60 change named in the update (anchor: 17–20 = outcome first, every item tied to the customer).

brevity_and_fluency.anchor: Every segment within ±5 s; one filler in 12.1 minutes, no tag questions, no long pauses (anchor: 13–15 = on time, fluent).

recovery.anchor: All three objections acknowledged → boundary → evidence → offer; follow-ups answered with artefacts (anchor: 9–10 = pattern held under follow-up).

stems: "Paid orders are arriving empty because…" — keep opening with the cost and the cause in one sentence.
"I re-planned: kept…, dropped…, moved…" — the three verbs made the T+90 checkpoint easy to follow; reuse them.
"The control is… and you can check it by…" — pair every governance claim with the artefact the listener can open.
previous_run_comparison: First recorded run for dryrun on lab 15 (scenario ghost-orders-eu); no previous run to compare with.
